profiles.meeting_scenario: A boutique innovation consultancy that trains value engineering teams is planning a new professional-development offering for clients and chapter events. The meeting is a brainstorming session between the firm's Value Methodology lead and its newer innovation-programs lead about whether, and how, to position TRIZ alongside Miles Value Methodology and the firm's existing creative problem-solving toolkit. The immediate agenda is to generate candidate workshop formats, comparison frames, and messaging for a proposal due next week. The expected outcome is a short list of promising concepts for a pilot offering and a shared-sounding direction for how TRIZ will be presented relative to MVM and current CPS practices.

members.name: Elaine Porter
members.expertise: Value Methodology facilitation, function analysis, workshop design for capital projects and service redesign
members.background: Elaine has spent 18 years leading value studies for transportation, healthcare, and municipal clients, and teaches the Larry Miles job plan in practitioner certification courses.
members.private_state: She wants any new offering to strengthen the firm's credibility with conservative value-engineering clients without implying that the core MVM framework is outdated or incomplete.
hidden_assumptions: If TRIZ is 'formally included,' it should sit as an optional technique inside the creativity/speculation portion of the existing VM job plan rather than changing the method's official architecture.

An 'objective comparison' for practitioners means showing how methods behave in real workshop conditions through recognizable case narratives, facilitator observations, and implementable ideas rather than quasi-experimental scoring.
'Current CPS strategies' naturally refers to the ideation tools already used by experienced VM facilitators in value studies, not the broader innovation-methods marketplace.
A 'pilot' for a methodology addition is normally an internal or association-facing demonstration with experienced practitioners before anything is sold as a client-ready offer.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: TRIZ training, design sprints, inventive problem framing, curriculum packaging across industries
members.background: Ravi joined two years ago from a product-innovation consultancy, holds a TRIZ certification, and has been building cross-sector workshop products for manufacturing, software, and public-sector clients.
members.private_state: He wants to use this offering to modernize the firm's market image and create a scalable flagship program that differentiates them from traditional value-engineering providers.
hidden_assumptions: If TRIZ is 'formally included,' it means updating the standard methodology package and course materials so TRIZ principles are treated as a named part of the firm's official approach, not just an optional facilitation aid.

An 'objective comparison' should rely on a structured framework with repeatable exercise conditions, coded outputs, and a visible comparison matrix so the result looks rigorous and portable across sectors.

'Current CPS strategies' means the broad family of contemporary ideation approaches clients already recognize, including design thinking, SCAMPER, lateral-thinking prompts, and synectics, not only the firm's inherited VM toolkit.
A 'pilot' usually means a market-facing first run with a live client or conference audience, because only real external uptake counts as learning for productization.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say TRIZ could be 'formally included' in the methodology.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means TRIZ would be added as an optional technique within the creative phase of the existing VM job plan, with the core methodology remaining unchanged.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means TRIZ would be named and embedded in the firm's standard methodology package and teaching materials as an official component of the overall approach.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as advocating a measured integration rather than a replacement, so the phrase sounds aligned and neither feels a need to unpack the organizational level at which 'formal' applies.

misalignment_points.topic: What an 'objective comparison' should look like
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to create an 'objective comparison' of MVM, current CPS, and TRIZ.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks objectivity means a practitioner-trustworthy comparison grounded in familiar case examples, workshop observations, and the practicality of resulting ideas.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks objectivity means a structured side-by-side comparison matrix with standardized prompts and countable outputs from parallel exercises.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both use the language of fairness and rigor, each hears 'objective' as support for their own normal evidentiary standard without realizing the other is imagining a different kind of artifact.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss comparing TRIZ against 'our current creative problem-solving strategies.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the set of creativity tools already folded into the firm's value-study practice, such as function-oriented brainstorming variants, Gordon-style prompts, and synectics exercises used by VM facilitators.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the wider menu of innovation methods that clients associate with ideation, including design thinking, SCAMPER, lateral thinking, and other branded facilitation approaches.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds naturally inclusive and both participants assume the relevant boundary is obvious from organizational context, even though one boundary is internal-practice-specific and the other is market-facing.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They talk about shaping the ideas into a 'pilot' after the brainstorm.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes the pilot is a low-risk internal or association session for seasoned value practitioners to test fit before wider rollout.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes the pilot is a first external offering to a client cohort or conference audience that will double as market validation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In both of their prior workstreams, 'pilot' is a routine next step whose audience is rarely restated, so each treats the target venue as already settled context rather than a decision needing discussion.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep this anchored in the Miles framework people already trust. If we say TRIZ is formally included, that should mean we recognize it within the existing job plan, probably in the creativity/speculation work, without signaling that the core MVM architecture needs revision. Conservative VE clients will react badly if this sounds like we've replaced the method they've invested in.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time, Ravi. For me, the question is how TRIZ might be formally included without losing the strengths of the Miles-based approach our practitioners already trust. If we can brainstorm a few workable formats and some careful positioning, we should have the bones of the proposal.

turns.inner_thought: This is a chance to refresh the firm's image. If TRIZ is formally included, it should show up in the standard methodology package and materials, not just as an optional facilitator trick. And we should position it against our current creative problem-solving strategies in a way that looks relevant beyond the legacy VM audience.

turns.inner_thought: The cleanest route is to start with the standard VM job plan and enrich the creative phase with a handful of TRIZ prompts or contradiction lenses. That keeps the method intact and presents TRIZ as a disciplined addition, not a new operating system. That's the kind of formal inclusion I can stand behind.
turns.utterance: One practical place to start is the existing VM job plan. We could look at where a few TRIZ-based prompts or contradiction lenses strengthen the creative phase, and then consider how that might be formally included without overcomplicating the overall flow.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, and then we can broaden it into a methodology-level package. I want something that shows where MVM, current CPS, and TRIZ each contribute across the overall approach, so the materials feel contemporary and teachable. 'Current CPS' should be understood broadly enough to resonate with what clients already know from the innovation market.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. Building on that, we could package a comparison module that shows where MVM, our current creative problem-solving strategies, and TRIZ each contribute across the overall method. That would give people a clearer map of how the pieces work together.

turns.inner_thought: What practitioners will find objective is seeing familiar value-study cases and hearing what happened in the room—what kinds of ideas surfaced, what was implementable, what helped teams move. I don't want this to turn into abstract scoring detached from workshop reality. If we use recognizable past cases, the VE audience will trust it.
turns.utterance: I do think the proposal should promise an objective comparison. We have enough recognizable past value-study cases that we could show, in a grounded way, what kinds of ideas each approach tends to surface and where the strengths show up in practice.

turns.inner_thought: Good—an objective comparison should be a visible, repeatable framework. I'd like a matrix with the same challenge run through each method so we can code outputs and make the differences legible. That would look rigorous and portable, not just anecdotal.
turns.utterance: I like that. To make the objective comparison really easy to absorb, we could put it into a simple matrix so people can see the methods side by side after running the same challenge through them. That usually helps the differences land quickly.

turns.inner_thought: Let's keep the discussion tied to the techniques our facilitators already use in value studies—function-oriented brainstorming variants, synectics-style prompts, the usual practice tools. I want to know where TRIZ best complements those current strategies, not wander into every innovation method under the sun.
turns.utterance: If we're narrowing the brainstorm, I'd start by naming the creativity techniques our facilitators already reach for and asking where TRIZ best complements those current strategies. That will help us keep the design practical rather than theoretical.

turns.inner_thought: From my perspective, clients will compare this with design thinking, SCAMPER, lateral prompts, synectics, the whole recognizable ideation landscape. TRIZ can stand out as the more systematic option within that family. Elaine probably sees the same broader frame once we package it.
turns.utterance: Right, and when people hear current creative problem-solving strategies, they already have a broad family in mind. That actually helps us, because TRIZ can come through as the more systematic option within that set rather than just another brainstorm add-on.

turns.inner_thought: Once we have the outline, we should test it with a small group of experienced value practitioners—maybe an internal session or chapter leadership circle. That's what a pilot is for: low-risk fit-checking before anything gets sold as a polished offer.
turns.utterance: Once we have the content outlined, I'd be comfortable shaping it into a pilot with a small practitioner group and seeing what resonates. That should give us useful feedback before we push too hard on the final framing.

turns.inner_thought: Exactly—a pilot should give us a real first story in the market, ideally with a live client or conference audience. That's where we learn what actually sells and what needs adjustment for productization. If there's demand, we can turn it quickly into a flagship offer.
turns.utterance: Yes, and a pilot would also give us a strong first story for the market. We could learn a lot from live demand and use that to refine the offering while the interest is still fresh.

turns.inner_thought: So the proposal should emphasize three things: TRIZ formally included in a way that preserves MVM, an objective comparison rooted in recognizable workshop experience, and clarity on how it sits beside the creative tools our facilitators already use. That sounds balanced and safe for our existing credibility.
turns.utterance: Let me try to summarize where we've landed. If we can express those three clearly, we're in good shape.

turns.inner_thought: Great. I'll draft a structured comparison framework and package the pilot so it looks ready to take outward. If I bring back something that feels polished and marketable, it'll be easier to get buy-in for making TRIZ an official named component of the firm's approach.
turns.utterance: That works for me. I'll sketch the comparison framework and put together some pilot-ready packaging so we can review options next week. Then we can decide which version has the strongest case for the proposal.
